title: Deployment Briefing: Hub Rotation Notes — Sep 14 2026
content:
Deployment Briefing: Hub Rotation — 2026-09-14

Purpose:
Quick sync for the on-call rotation handoff across Concierge -> Field Install -> Customer Ops. Capture short incident notes, mitigations applied during the shift, and outstanding blockers to escalate to Platform and SRE. This is a working doc: add new findings as you triage.

Attendees:
- Aisha (rotation lead)
- Evan (field concierge)
- Lina (obs/SRE)
- Carlos (solutions engineer on Acadia Health)
- On-call: Jonas (night)

Summary (high level):
- Shift experienced three customer-impacting events during morning window (06:00-10:30 PDT). Two resolved with mitigations; one remains open and is functionally a customer blocker (Acadia VPC egress routing causing model shard fetch failures).
- Observability blind spot for model shard rehydrate errors surfaced (metrics missing for kernel-level OOM in dedicated nodes). Lina to file follow-up with infra team.

Incident 1: TLS cert rotation race — reduced connectivity to onprem control channel (resolved)
- Symptoms: ~25% of management control-plane requests from site agents to the hub returned 502 over 12m. Customer-side (HVB Corp) reported intermittent failures to fetch rollout configs.
- Timeline: 06:12 small spike in 502s -> 06:16 automatic retry thrash -> 06:24 recovery after manual restart of hub-agent (restart triggered by field concierge).
- Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous cert rolling + agent cache mismatch. Old cert still trusted in some agent pools, new cert presented by hub; small subset of older agents failed TLS handshake due to SNI pathing.
- Mitigation applied: forced agent restart on affected pools via /opt/redwood/bin/hub-agent restart; rolled back cert rotation window for 20m while we coordinated with infra.
- Next steps: add pre-rotation probe that tests representative agent pools (Evan). Add a 60s jitter to cert-rollover orchestration (Platform infra ticket ENG-4907).

Incident 2: Model shard prefetch OOM on GPU slice (transient, resolved)
- Symptoms: Onprem node node-az3-gpu-07 started rejecting shard load requests; pod restarted twice in 18m. Observed GPU memory pressure >95% and kernel OOM logs.
- Actions taken: disabled aggressive prefetch in node config (prefetch.max_concurrent=2) and forced KV cache warm-up to a slower policy. Restarted shard loader processes.
- Root cause: aggressive prefetch + larger-than-expected batch of long-context requests from internal load tests. Prefetch combined with warm KV caches exhausted reserved GPU memory on that slice.
- Follow-ups: tune prefetching defaults for onprem with small capacity customers; create new quantization profile for 2x64GB nodes (owner: Lina, due 2026-09-21). Add explicit mem watermark alerts to Prometheus rule group.

Incident 3 (open): Acadia Health — VPC egress/nat rule blocking model shard fetches (customer blocker)
- Symptoms: Several model fetches and container pulls failing with TCP RST when reaching our artifact mirror (s3-compatible) from customer VPC. Error seen as TLS handshake timeout and connection reset.
- Evidence: Packet capture from customer border shows SYN then RST from intermediate NAT gateway. Customer reports recent firewall rule change for outbound 443 to only allowed CIDR ranges (policy change last week).
- Temporary workaround attempted: tunnel proxy via customer-managed bastion (increased latency ~300ms) — successful but unacceptable for SLOs.
- Current state: customer has paused production rollout until outbound rule updated. This is blocking 3 scheduled installs this week.
- Owner: Carlos (SE) coordinating with Acadia networking. Escalation: request a short-term exception to allow our artifact mirror CIDR 52.24.78.0/24 or provide signed S3 origin certificate to allow a different egress path (suggested).
- Suggested escalation path: Sales+Customer Success to request exception; Security runbook: require egress audit and timestamped approval.

Observability & telemetry notes:
- Missing metric: "shard_load_failure_reason" is not emitted when kernel OOM occurs; logs show only generic container exit. Lina to open ENG-4918 to instrument kernel OOM detection into loader and export reason as a label.
- Alert fatigue: several low-value alerts firing during prefetch bursts. Propose a temporary suppression rule for prefetch-related transient OOM alerts in non-prod clusters (Aisha to prototype).

Preflight checklist additions (quick proposals):
- Add VPC egress CIDR verification step for customers that pin outbound rules (explicit inputs at intake form).
- Add a lightweight cert rotation probe that exercises management API and the agent pool matrix prior to window.
- Add an optional small-sample stress test runner for onprem installs that simulates long-context requests to validate prefetch defaults.

Operational runes / snippet notes (for runbook entry):
- Check agent connectivity: sudo journalctl -u hub-agent -n 200 | grep -i "tls"
- Restart hub agent: sudo systemctl restart hub-agent && sleep 30 && sudo systemctl status hub-agent
- Lower prefetch flag (runtime): curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"prefetch.max_concurrent":2}' http://localhost:3100/api/v1/runtime-config
- Example log excerpt (sanitized):
  [2026-09-14T06:18:23Z] shard-loader[pid=4221] ERROR: kernel OOM while allocating 1.2GB for kv-cache -> exit_code=137

Outstanding blockers and ask list:
- Acadia outbound exception (P0 for customer). Need Sales+CS pressure and temporary cert-to-cert path if they won't open egress. (Owner: Carlos, Escalate: Sales/CS)
- Instrumentation for kernel OOM reasons (Owner: Lina, Ticket: ENG-4918)
- Cert rotation precheck probe implementation (Owner: Evan, spike due 2026-09-20)

Action items (owners + target dates):
- Carlos: get written exception or alternate artifact host from Acadia — target 2026-09-16 (P0).
- Lina: open ENG-4918 and implement export of shard_load_failure_reason; add memory watermark alerts — target 2026-09-21.
- Evan: prototype cert rotation precheck probe and runbook step with 60s jitter — target 2026-09-20.
- Aisha: prototype alert suppression for prefetch transient OOM in non-prod; coordinate with SRE — target 2026-09-18.
- Platform Infra (ENG-4907): add jitter to cert rotation orchestration window (assigned to infra, please confirm ETA).

Notes for next rotation:
- Hand off with current state of Acadia ticket and any new packet captures. If no exception by 09-16 close loop with Solutions + Sales for temporary signed artifact host.
- If further prefetch OOMs appear, escalate to Serving Runtime lead for a fast patch to the loader memory accounting.

Misc (quick thoughts):
- Consider adding a small public artifact mirror (read-only) specifically for installs that pin outbound egress; mirrors could be regionally scoped and advertised in onboarding to reduce ad-hoc NAT exceptions. Cost estimate rough: $1k/mo per region for small bandwidth expected in first year.

Appendix: recent related tickets referenced:
- ENG-4823: onprem install preflight failures (linked above)
- ENG-4907: cert rotation jockeying (infra)
- ENG-4918: (proposed) kernel OOM instrumentation

End of briefing. Add hands-on notes below as you triage.
